'''Amos Brittain Smith III''' (August 26, 1944 – February 3, 2025) was an American chemist and academic who was a professor at the [[University of Pennsylvania]].

==Life and career==
Smith is most notable for his research in the total synthesis of complex natural products, as well as the chemistry of [[mammal]]ian [[pheromones]]<ref name="Smith Ott pp. 13095–13096">{{cite journal | last1=Smith | first1=Amos B. | last2=Ott | first2=Gregory R. | title=Total Synthesis of (−)-Macrolactin A | journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=118 | issue=51 | date=1 January 1996 | issn=0002-7863 | doi=10.1021/ja963543a | pages=13095–13096| bibcode=1996JAChS.11813095S }}</ref> and chemical communication.

He held a co-appointment at the [[Monell Chemical Senses Center]]<ref name=monell>{{cite web|url=http://monell.org/Faculty/SmithA.htm|title=Scientific Staff|publisher=Monell Chemical Senses Center|accessdate=August 6, 2008| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20080905224349/http://www.monell.org/Faculty/SmithA.htm| archivedate= 5 September 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref> and held the Rhodes-Thompson Professorship of Chemistry at the [[University of Pennsylvania]]'s department of chemistry.<ref name=penn>{{cite web|url=http://absmithgroup.chem.upenn.edu/absgroup/ |title=The Smith Research Group |publisher=University of Pennsylvania, Department of Chemistry |accessdate=August 6, 2008 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080719123054/http://absmithgroup.chem.upenn.edu/absgroup/ |archivedate=19 July 2008 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Amos B. Smith III was a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and member of the [[ESPCI|ESPCI ParisTech]] Scientific Council.<ref>[http://www.espci.fr/actu/081117_ISC.pdf ESPCI ParisTech ISC] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081126040128/http://www.espci.fr/actu/081117_ISC.pdf |date=November 26, 2008 }}</ref>

In 2015, he was awarded the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]'s [[Perkin Prize for Organic Chemistry]] "for his continued outstanding contributions to new organic reaction development, complex natural product total synthesis, and new small molecules for medicinal chemistry".<ref name="RSC-2015">{{cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/PerkinPrize/2015-Winner.asp|title=RSC Perkin Prize for Organic Chemistry 2015 Winner|date=5 May 2015|publisher=[[Royal Society of Chemistry]]|accessdate=26 May 2015}}</ref>

Smith died on February 3, 2025, at the age of 80.<ref>{{cite web |title=Amos Brittain Smith III |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/name/amos-smith-iii-obituary?id=57461815 |website=Legacy |access-date=6 February 2025}}</ref>
